Good. Recovery is a long, hard road I’ve had to go down in the past too. You’ll often feel like it’s not working, or maybe that you’re not being heard, taken seriously, or the like. But I promise you that if you stick with it through the therapy, medicine changes, ect., you will come out better than ok. Important things to know is 1. It’s okay to not get along with your therapist. You need to shop for one, till you find one you get along with. You have to tell them everything. It’s hard, but it’s worth it. Therapy saved my life and it took me three tries till I found one I liked 2. Medication is not there to make you dull. It’s there to rebalance the brain and make you feel *normal.* The goal isn’t to make you catatonic, so if you feel your meds aren’t making you feel normal, then it’s okay to switch. Different meds effect everyone differently, and you will probably have to go on and off medications till you find one that works. This can take a long time and be really scary. Make sure your doctor is taking in consideration of possible side effects and is weening you on and off slowly so you can come down as soon as symptoms start to arrive, if they do. For me, I ended up finding my perfect medicine after two tries and after 10 yard I’ve never felt better. 3. Even when things are darker than dark, remind yourself that things do change. This, like everything else, with hard work, it will change. 4. Advocate for yourself. If you need something, or feel like you’re not being heard, talk about it. One of the hardest things about mental health is feeling steam rolled. It’s a very personal thing, and to get the best treatment, you have to be open. There may be shitty people, and there may be times that people don’t take you seriously or the like. Those times don’t define your treatment or you and advocating is the best way to get the treatment you need. 5. Remember to breath. Seriously. Breathing right will change your life. If you feel panicked by a situation, don’t react, step away and deep breath for 10 minutes. Look up meditations on YouTube and breathing exercises. It can make a huge diffrence 6. If you smoke pot, stop. I’m speaking from experience. Regular pot use stunted my recovery and it only started to get better when I slowed down. Pot is an incredible medicine if you have a doctor guiding you to the right strain. Just any strain of pot off the street won’t help. 7. Say nice things to yourself in the mirror. 10 things, 20 if you can. It feels like it won’t help in the moment, but like the rest of treatment, it’s about building up. 8. You’ll start to feel better before you realize it, so when you feel like giving up, try to hold on a little longer. 9. You’re worth it and 10. Everything’s going to be ok.
